18.text: for the hand. Its length is from 50 cm. to 70 cm. The women, when using

20.text: force upon the spread skin. They work alternately with the right and left

22.text: on the same cover, since one alone would find it difficult to stretch and

23.text: manage the heavy skin cover. The beating-out of the frost requires con-

24.text: siderable strength, and during the whole winter forms the most difficult task

25.text: of the Reindeer Chukchee woman. However, in the coldest season it is

26.text: hardly possible to omit a single day’s beating, because, if the sleeping-room

27.text: is not beaten out, it will become damp the next night, and even drip with

28.text: moisture. This continual change from damp to frost, and the severe daily

29.text: beating, cause the cover of the inner room to wear down rapidly.

33.text: The two halves of the outer cover require about forty large skins. The

34.text: cover of the inner room is made of from twelve to fifteen skins. For the

35.text: beds ten large skins are required. Each sleeping-room is occupied by a separate

36.text: family, and belongs to one woman, who takes care of it. There are sometimes

37.text: two sleeping-rooms in the same tent, but this is not very often the case.

38.text: Usually the sleeping-room is in the rear of the tent, facing the entrance, which

39.text: is generally toward the northeast (Morning Dawn¹), occasionally toward the
